purpose: Full factory missions at50/200/1000/5000, paired narrower openings, and declared numerical refinements. Preserve incomplete/contact outcomes.
method: Genuine local Boids, common broad route guidance, same local avoidance heuristic, no individual trajectories or scheduling. Airflow off; ideal observations. Primary step2.5ms,100Hz control.180s fixed horizon. No gain tuning after outcomes.
geometry: Original5×4m doorways versus3×2.5m doorways; same door centers, route and other solids. Geometry narrowing tested at50/200, not extrapolated to5000.
initialization: Same jittered3D lattice at0.75m spacing, cross-section caps16×9, larger count grows initial volume. Fresh seeds1501/1502. Large counts have one primary seed, not statistical safety assurance.
numerics: Full2.5→1.25ms comparisons at200/narrow and1000/wide: same count/stop, end difference<.01s and max final position difference<.01m.5000 comparison covers only first20s, matched against the coarse mission checkpoint; it cannot validate later full-mission dynamics. Missing checkpoint due earlier stop is reported, never treated as a pass.
recording: Float64LE exact positions/quaternions every1s and at terminal contact. Scientific samples every0.1s; swept contact checks every physics step. Streamed binary avoids large in-memory replay arrays. Full17-state endpoints and20/60/120/180s checkpoints retained. Visual interpolation is not a collision detector.
changes: Conservative obstacle broadphase excludes only boxes farther than the original1.6m clearance activation along at least one axis, with1e-10 guard. Neighbor distance removes temporary arrays but keeps arithmetic. Equivalence checks compare exact old final states and metrics through5000 bodies.
timing: Three concurrent numerical child processes. Mission wall times include recording and are descriptive, not an isolated scaling benchmark. Milestone25 provides the separately measured baseline. No paid compute.
limits: 180s simulation horizon only; no success forced by resetting, teleporting or deleting drones. Completed drones keep flying. One contact stops entire run; other unfinished drones are not independent collisions.
